    <div class="container title">
        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <div class="container title">
        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>

    <div class="container title">
        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <div class="container title">
        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

    <div class="container title">
        <div class="row clearfix">
            <div class="column full">
                <h1>Get&nbsp;Involved</h1>
                
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <section class='page_content'>
        <div class='container'>
            <div class='row clearfix'>
                <div class='column full'>
                    <figure>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://www.openhub.net/p/gimp/widgets/project_basic_stats?format=js'></script>
</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

</figure>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </section>

<p><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is <span class="help" title="software that may be modified and distributed
freely, as long as you do not deny other users these freedoms">Free
Software</span>, mostly licensed under the <a href="/about/COPYING"><span class="caps">GNU</span> General Public License
(<span class="caps">GPL</span>)</a> license, and historically part of the <a href="https://www.gnu.org/"><span class="caps">GNU</span>
Project</a>.</p>
<p>In the free software world, there is generally no distinction between users and
developers. As in a <strong>friendly neighbourhood</strong>, everybody pitches in to help their
neighbors. Please consider the time you give in assistance to others as&nbsp;payment.</p>
<p>Ways in which you can&nbsp;help:</p>
<dl>
<dt><a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/submit-patch/">Fix bugs or program</a> new&nbsp;features</dt>
<dd>Our <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/">Developer Website</a> is where you want to
start learning about being a code&nbsp;contributor.</dd>
<dt>Report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a> (errors in the&nbsp;program)</dt>
<dd><span class="caps">GIMP</span> is not bug-free nor is any other application so <a href="/bugs/">reporting bugs</a>
that you encounter is very important to the development, it helps the developers
to make <span class="caps">GIMP</span> more stable. You don&#8217;t have to be a developer or a everyday user
to report&nbsp;bugs.</dd>
<dt>Test existing features and provide&nbsp;feedback</dt>
<dd>If you think a feature can be improved somehow, you can discuss the
improvements on the <a href="/discuss.html#mailing-lists"><code>gimp-gui</code> mailing list</a> and
create enhancement requests (the same way you report <a href="/bugs/">bugs</a>).</dd>
<dt>Write or improve the <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/">documentation</a></dt>
<dd>The <a href="https://docs.gimp.org/help.html">Documentation websites tells you all about
contributing</a>.</dd>
<dt>Translate <span class="caps">GIMP</span> or documentation to your own&nbsp;language</dt>
<dd>Contact the respective <a href="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>

</html>https://www.gimp.org/develop="https://l10n.gnome.org/teams/">translator team</a> for
your language. The <a href="https://wiki.gnome.org/TranslationProject">Translation
Project</a> page of <span class="caps">GNOME</span> is also of&nbsp;interest.</dd>
<dt>Write <a href="/tutorials/">tutorials</a> on this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>We have a <a href="/tutorials/#contributing-new-tutorials-or-fixes">procedure for writing tutorials</a>&nbsp;too!</dd>
<dt>Improve this&nbsp;website</dt>
<dd>Creating websites that contain useful information is very important. It is
just as important as doing bug reports. A website contains a lot of information
that are needed for the development to move on and it also contains information
that will help the public to understand what the application is all about. We
explain how to help us <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/wgo/">in a dedicated
tutorial</a>.</dd>
<dt>Make artwork for <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>After all, <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is for artists, designers, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

</html>https://www.gimp.org/developdesigners, photographers and other creators.
So if you want to contribute your art under a Libre license, feel free to <a href="/discuss.html">reach
out</a>.</dd>
<dt>Let people know you used <span class="caps">GIMP</span> for your&nbsp;artwork</dt>
<dd>On your website, social networks or&nbsp;whatnot!</dd>
<dt>Give away copies of <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>This is Free Software, it is made to be shared, just like knowledge and
know-how. Give <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to your neighbours, your friend, your family,&nbsp;everyone!</dd>
<dt>Help others to learn <span class="caps">GIMP</span></dt>
<dd>Write <a href="/books/">books about <span class="caps">GIMP</span></a>, teach it <a href="/news/2018/11/08/gimp-2-10-8-released/#gimp-in-universite-de-cergy-pontoise">in
university</a>,
in websites, video tutorial, local community workshops, everywhere! <span class="caps">GIMP</span> is free
to use and will never try to tamper with your&nbsp;work.</dd>
<dt>Help new <span class="caps">GIMP</span> users in online&nbsp;forums</dt>
<dd>See the <a href="https://www.gimp.org/discuss.html">Discuss</a> page for a list of
official discussion venues for <span class="caps">GIMP</span>. Helping in non-official forums, for
instance in your native language is also&nbsp;great!</dd>
<dt>etc.</dt>
<dd>As you can see, anyone can help. This is what a community is&nbsp;about.</dd>
</dl>
<p>Once you&#8217;ve figured out what to do, be bold and get to&nbsp;work!</p>
<p>The <span class="caps">GIMP</span> community is a friendly one, but it probably is still worth saying this: Try not to take critiques personally. We all just want <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to be the best that it can be. Once approved, your edits will be merged into the code base, making you an official <span class="caps">GIMP</span> contributor. And if you keep up the good work, not only will this process get easier with practice, your administrative privileges in <span class="caps">GIMP</span> development will also increase&nbsp;too.</p>
<h2 id="development-status">Development Status<a class="headerlink" href="#development-status" title="Permanent link">&para;</a></h2>
<p>The team is currently busy working on v3.0. This will be a port of <span class="caps">GIMP</span> to
<span class="caps">GTK</span>+3, much newer and better supported version of the user interface&nbsp;toolkit.</p>
<p>A huge part of <span class="caps">GIMP</span>&#8217;s source code is related to the user interface, so this port
is a major undertaking, especially since we shall break <span class="caps">API</span> and refactor
numerous parts of the&nbsp;program.</p>
<p>We still need to port more plugins to become <span class="caps">GEGL</span> operations. If you are willing
to help with that, please refer to the <a href="https://wiki.gimp.org/index.php/Hacking:Porting_filters_to_GEGL">Porting filters to <span class="caps">GEGL</span></a>
page to see what you could work&nbsp;on.</p>
<p>To get a better understanding of where the project is heading to, which features
are planned etc., please visit the <a href="https://developer.gimp.org/core/roadmap/">Roadmap</a>&nbsp;page.</p>
                </div>
